artifacts.how: agy changelog > internal/cli/testdata/changelog_reference.txt, then update the five constants in internal/cli/changelog_data_test.go (byte length, line count, section count, bullet count, sha256) and regenerate this lock. At 1.4.6 the newest section is 1.4.5 — the 1.4.6 release notes are not in the changelog feed yet

the full system prompt of a live agy 1.4.6 request body, recorded through the cycle-274 capture wrapper (cmd/agy + devutils/agyproxy). It is the reference for every static section: 1.4.6 added <terminal_sandbox> (second position) and one <guidelines> bullet. To refresh: re-record a request body against the new binary, then rebuild internal/agyprompt/sections/*.txt from it

re-recorded alongside capture_1.4.6.txt in the same proxy run; it carries the os_version / workspaces / subagents / skills / user_rules inputs Build() is fed. The 1.4.4 pair stays on disk as the previous release's evidence

the <user_rules> block of a controlled probe request body. The block's own bytes are from 1.4.5; the rendering it pins was re-verified at 1.4.6 by the byte-identity of the whole 70,853-byte prompt (capture_1.4.6.txt) — preamble wording, user_global labels, plugin rules and the 24 KB truncation marker included

agy -p='x' --output-format stream-json and collect the init.tools array; repeat from three working directories as the cycle-275 test does. Re-verified at 1.4.6: sixty names, byte-identical to the 1.4.3/1.4.5 capture

capture a streamGenerateContent body (cmd/agy wrapper or a CLOUD_CODE_URL mock) and extract request.tools[0].functionDeclarations; it must stay twelve, in the captured order, with the same required fields. 1.4.6 added the run_command BypassSandbox boolean. The 1.4.5 and 1.4.4 captures remain on disk as the previous releases' evidence

run the real 1.4.4 TUI with CLOUD_CODE_URL pointed at a mock that answers the first streamGenerateContent with one functionCall, then read functionResponse.response.output in the follow-up request; redo for read_file (whole/range/empty), write_file (create/refusal/append) and edit_file (single/multi-line). NOT re-captured at 1.4.6 — it needs a tool-using turn under a pty harness

run the real agy TUI in a workspace with .agents/agents/<name>.md and --agent <name>; answer the first streamGenerateContent with a CLOUD_CODE_URL mock, then extract request.tools[*].functionDeclarations. It must stay seven, in order, and keep toolSummary/toolAction required. Re-verified at 1.4.6: identical, schedule included

extract the uncompressed FileDescriptorProto for google/gca/aicode/v1main/remote_agent_proxy.proto from the agy binary (see out/local-macos/protos/README.md) and emit one <RPC>\t<Request>\t<Response> line per method; TestReferenceRPCMethodsMatchFixture pins the order. Seventy-seven methods at 1.4.6 (1.4.6 appended SearchFiles, StartLocalPluginSignIn, CompleteLocalPluginSignIn, CreateAgent and GetAgent); the 1.4.5 and 1.4.4 captures remain on disk as the previous releases' evidence

decode the FileDescriptorProto at the offset named in out/local-macos/protos/README.md with descriptor_pb2 and print it with text_format; the offset moves on every agy release, and the naive top-level field walk overshoots the public descriptor — the syntax:"proto3" marker is the reliable end

same procedure as remote_agent_proxy_1.4.6.txt, for third_party/jetski/remote_agent_proxy_pb/remote_agent_proxy.proto (package exa.remote_agent_proxy_pb). The internal descriptor did not change at 1.4.6 — the file is byte-identical to the 1.4.5 capture

cd rea-go-seeds && mkdir -p <outdir> && go run . ~/.local/bin/agy <outdir>. Every address moves on every agy release, so the Ghidra project (out/local-macos/proj) and the decompiled output (out/local-macos/dec/) have to be rebuilt from this file; the committed decompile reports carry the addresses this file held when they were written
written by the same rea-go-seeds run as seeds.txt; the leaf-name inventory used by out/local-macos/find_callers.py and out/local-macos/xref/analyze.py
